title: Weight Thaw Orchestrator and KV Accelerant Scheduler for Faster Dedicated Startups
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem statement:
Customers on Dedicated fleets observe 3–12s P95 cold-start tails when switching model variants or scaling up a replica. This increases request latency and burns GPU startup cycles, impacting both SLOs and committed throughput economics. Current warm-pool behavior seeds weights and KV cache statically which leads to unnecessary full-weight fetches and KV thrash when traffic patterns are bursty.

Goal:
Design and implement a Weight Thaw Orchestrator combined with a KV Accelerant Scheduler that reduces cold-start tails by: 1) prioritizing partial weight thawing based on estimated request hotpaths (thaw windows), 2) coordinating KV proxy prefetches for predicted token prefixes, and 3) integrating autoscaling budget tokens so prewarm actions respect committed throughput guarantees and do not exceed reserved capacity budgets.

Key capabilities to deliver:
- Weight Thaw Orchestrator: progressive weight load that stages parameter groups (embedding, attention, MLP) in order of earliest-requested layers with a fallback to full load. Supports soft-freeze eviction bands to avoid noisy eviction during transient bursts.
- KV Accelerant Scheduler: short-lived prefetch jobs that prime KV shards for likely token prefixes, with per-tenant priority and admission control to avoid eviction storms.
- Throughput Commitment Lanes: tie prewarm priority to tenant throughput commitments so that customers with higher committed lanes get earlier/priority thaw and KV accelerant slots.
- Autoscaling Policy Hooks: expose budget tokens and prewarm quotas to the autoscaler so scale-up decisions include the estimated residual warm-up time in scheduling.
- Fleet Controls and Observability: add overlays for residency maps, thaw progress metrics, and prewarm cost accounting in the Console (token-level and GPU-time costs).

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive prefetching improves latency but raises GPU and network I/O costs; mitigated by quota-based admission and tenant priority.
- Fine-grained weight thawing reduces perceived cold starts but increases complexity in kernel scheduling and memory fragmentation. We'll evaluate a hybrid chunked thaw (layer groups) approach before moving to per-parameter strategies.
- Prefetch correctness vs. privacy: KV prefetches are limited to non-sensitive prefixes and respect tenant isolation; any prefetch that touches encrypted payloads will be disabled by default.

Success metrics (initial):
- P95 startup latency reduction from baseline by >= 50% for scale-up and model-variant attach flows.
- Reduction in full-weight fetch operations per attach by >= 60%.
- Prewarm-induced extra GPU-seconds under steady-state < 5% of committed capacity per tenant.
- No increase in error rate or TLS/permission violations from prefetching logic.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Spec & Emulator (2 wks): design thaw sequences, define KV accelerant admission API; implement a simulator to measure thaw sequences impact on token-latency distribution.
2) Scheduler & Admission Control (3 wks): implement KV Accelerant Scheduler, admission API for autoscaler to request budget tokens.
3) Progressive Thaw Runtime (4 wks): implement staged weight loader in runtime with overlays for soft-freeze and residency map. Add efficient checkpoint diffing to avoid full re-pulls.
4) Integration & Observability (2 wks): surface thaw progress, prewarm costs, and tenant-level dashboards; add tracing hooks for thaw events.
5) Canary & Rollout (2 wks): canary on a subset of fleets, measure metrics, iterate on admission thresholds.

Rollout plan and safety:
- Start with non-critical tenants and internal load tests. Default KV accelerant admission to opt-in per-tenant.
- Implement conservative default quotas and a fast rollback flag that stops all prewarm jobs and drains thaw threads gracefully.
- Monitor GPU memory fragmentation and kernel time; escalate if fragmentation increases > 8% over baseline.

Open design questions / TODOs:
- Optimal chunk size for weight thawing: experiment with per-layer vs per-block thresholds.
- Admission token calibration: how many tokens per committed throughput unit yields best latency vs cost balance?
- Grace period heuristics for soft-freeze eviction bands.
- Evaluate interactions with existing KV snapshot seeding (see ENG-12845): should we unify snapshot indexes?

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end canary shows P95 start latency reduction >= 50% and no >1% increase in request errors.
- Autoscaler queries return prewarm ETA and budget token usage, and scale decisions account for estimated residual warmup time.
- Console displays per-tenant prewarm cost and thaw progress traces.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for scheduler admission and token accounting.
- Integration tests with runtime loader under synthetic traffic shapes (spike, gradual ramp, long-tail).
- Chaos test: simulate eviction storms and ensure graceful degrade to full load without correctness regression.
- Load test: measure GPU seconds overhead for prewarm under 1k tenant-equivalent traffic.

Operational runbook (summary):
- If prewarm causes capacity pressure: reduce prewarm admission tokens by 50% and revert to passive snapshot seeding.
- If memory fragmentation detected: pause progressive thaw and force a coalesced load; notify infra team.
- If prefetch increases error rate: disable KV accelerant for affected tenant and collect trace.

Longer-term ideas (for follow-ups):
- Predictive prewarm using historical traffic embeddings to select thaw sequences.
- Cross-tenant cooperative warm pools for best-effort free capacity reuse without breaching isolation.
- Hardware-aware thaw ordering using kernel latency models per GPU family.
